papers.title: Bayesian hierarchical uncertainty quantification of a helical-path tortuosity predictor for modeling hydraulic conductivity in sandstone aquifers
papers.abstract: Hydraulic conductivity and effective diffusivity in saturated sandstone aquifers depend on the square of tortuosity, so using a point estimate of tortuosity leaves its contribution to uncertainty unquantified in groundwater-flow and contaminant-transport models. A Bayesian hierarchical framework quantifies uncertainty in a published helical-path tortuosity predictor using a dataset of 51 sandstone samples spanning three formation classes: Tight German sandstones, clean Fontainebleau-analogous sandstones, and unconsolidated high-connectivity sandstones. The framework propagates uncertainty to hydrogeological quantities using the existing model and published data. Posterior predictions of tortuosity agree with the observations, with a mean absolute percentage error of approximately 3.3% and conservatively calibrated predictive intervals. Convergence was assessed using rank-normalized split $$\widehat{R}$$ R ^ , effective sample sizes, and autocorrelation times, and out-of-sample performance was assessed using Pareto-smoothed importance-sampling leave-one-out and five-fold cross-validation (held-out mean absolute percentage error near 5.1%). Fixing the class critical porosities at their published values and inferring them yield statistically indistinguishable predictions, with information-criterion differences within two paired standard errors; the comparison is a robustness check, and the published thresholds remain within the credible intervals under widened and flat priors, although the data constrain them mainly from above. The tortuosity posterior is then propagated into the formation factor, the effective diffusivity and a multiplicative hydraulic-conductivity uncertainty factor, and an ensemble of one-dimensional transport simulations converts these into 90% envelopes on contaminant plume extent and on diffusive breakthrough time through a low-permeability layer, providing uncertainty bounds for models of the sandstone classes studied.

papers.title: A comprehensive review and unified taxonomy of intelligent hybrid fractional-order models incorporated with machine learning in healthcare applications
papers.abstract: Fractional-order differential equations (FDEs) describe memory and hereditary effects that integer-order models cannot capture, while machine-learning (ML) methods extract patterns from large and noisy clinical data but often lack mechanistic meaning. Combining the two has become an active research direction in healthcare, yet the literature is spread across many disease areas and there is no common way to describe how the coupling is actually implemented. This review addresses that gap. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched PubMed and OpenAlex for journal articles published between January 2018 and March 2026 and used Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for citation searching. After screening 209 records, 43 hybrid FDE–ML studies were included. We propose a two-level taxonomy in which three coupling types (ML-informed estimation of fractional parameters; fractional physics-informed neural networks (FPINNs) and neural solvers; and fractional preprocessing of features) describe the mathematical link, and a fourth type describes the deployment layer (simulation engine and clinician-facing interface). We define a hybrid operator Q with an explicit domain and range that expresses every reviewed model as a composition of these components, and we illustrate it on the public UCI Dermatology dataset using repeated stratified cross-validation, baseline classifiers, and bootstrap confidence intervals. The evidence tables show that FPINNs and neural solvers dominate infectious-disease modelling, whereas oncology and cardiometabolic studies more often combine several types. Reported gains are study-specific, so we present them as representative values rather than pooled effects. We also discuss computational cost, data scarcity, uncertainty quantification, regulatory validation, and fairness. The main contribution of the work is a reproducible classification and a formal operator that can guide model selection, reporting, and validation in future hybrid fractional–ML studies in healthcare.

papers.abstract: Healthcare Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) security and blockchain consent governance remain siloed: intrusion detection systems monitor network traffic but ignore blockchain transaction anomalies, while blockchain anomaly detectors largely target general financial contexts. We propose the Blockchain-Enabled Cybersecurity Framework (BECF), a benchmark-validated architectural proof-of-concept that integrates temporally validated, SHAP-explainable gradient boosting for intrusion detection on ToN-IoT, probability-calibrated blockchain anomaly detection on Elliptic, smart-contract consent management on Ethereum Sepolia, and a composite risk function fusing network intrusion probability, blockchain anomaly probability, and patient data sensitivity. Fusion weights and classifiers are optimized through constrained grid search and Bayesian optimization, with bootstrap confidence intervals and controlled post-hoc comparisons. On ToN-IoT, the Bayesian-optimized LightGBM classifier achieves 99.89% accuracy (95% CI: [99.85%, 99.92%]), F1 = 0.9993, and MCC = 0.9969; on Elliptic, LightGBM achieves 76.63% balanced accuracy, F1 = 0.6290, and AUPRC = 0.5854 for general illicit Bitcoin transaction detection—not healthcare-consent attack detection. Smart contracts achieve 99.8% success, zero critical findings from the applied analyzers, and approximately 17.8% gas savings. Across 10,000 controlled integration-test events, BECF achieves a 74.4% event-level true positive rate for dual-layer alerts with a false-positive rate of 0.20%, and detects all 47 explicitly constructed coordinated scenarios (47/47; 100%; 95% Wilson CI: [92.4%, 100%]). These scenarios were generated in a controlled integration testbed and do not represent naturally occurring clinical attacks; therefore, the scenario result is controlled feasibility evidence rather than clinical detection performance. Prospective hospital validation and Ethereum-native attack validation remain necessary before clinical deployment.

papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital educational technologies has transformed the possibilities for science teaching, inclusive learning, and professional development. However, meaningful integration requires more than access to digital resources; it requires pedagogical judgment, sensitivity to learner diversity, effective learning strategies, and ethical responsibility. This thematic paper examines the integration of digital pedagogical tools and inclusive teaching practices in B.Ed. science teacher education in the context of India’s National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. Drawing on recent literature, international competency frameworks, inclusive education principles, and Indian educational policy, the paper develops five interconnected themes: purposeful digital pedagogy, inclusive science lesson design, learner-centred strategies, professional ethics in technology use, and institutional support for responsible digital transformation. It proposes an original conceptual framework, the Inclusive Digital Science Pedagogy and Ethics (IDSPE) Framework, which connects technology selection, accessibility, active learning, ethical decision-making, and reflective professional practice. The paper argues that digital tools can support differentiated instruction, scientific visualization, collaborative inquiry, and formative assessment when they are selected according to educational purpose and learner needs. At the same time, inaccessible platforms, digital inequality, inaccurate AI-generated content, privacy risks, and overdependence on automated systems may undermine inclusive educational goals. The paper recommends integrating digital competence, universal design, responsible AI literacy, and reflective ethical practice into B.Ed. science curricula. It concludes that the success of educational technology under NEP 2020 should be judged not by the quantity of tools used but by their contribution to equitable participation, meaningful scientific understanding, and responsible professional practice.

papers.title: Two-stage attention-guided active learning for nonstationary Gaussian process modeling in robust parameter design
papers.abstract: Robust parameter design is vital for continuous quality improvement in industrial practice. However, modeling nonstationary response surfaces with limited data remains challenging because insufficient predictive accuracy may introduce optimistic bias in estimating optimal parameter settings. We propose a two-stage attention-inspired active learning method within a nonstationary Gaussian process (NSGP) modeling framework for robust parameter design. This two-stage acquisition first ranks candidates by expected quality loss and then applies a maximin rule to preserve subset diversity. In the first stage, candidate design points are ranked by their relevance to the specified target region, and a subset with high relevance scores is selected for further refinement. In the second stage, spatial diversity is enforced by selecting additional points from this subset to mitigate clustering. The selected points are used to update the training set and NSGP model. A genetic algorithm solves the NSGP-based robust parameter design problem and determines optimal settings. Comparisons with classical design baselines and three modern acquisition criteria show that the proposed method improves predictive accuracy and enhances the robustness of solutions under limited data. The effectiveness of the method is further supported by ablation experiments, target-value sensitivity analysis, and a modified 10-variable Wing Weight analytical benchmark.

papers.title: A Unified Ornstein–Uhlenbeck–Lévy–Branching Framework for Interpretable Modeling of Cancer Evolution
papers.abstract: Biological evolution arises from the interplay of continuous stochastic dynamics, discontinuous transitions, branching-associated diversification, environmental perturbations, and imperfect experimental observations. Existing stochastic models—including Brownian motion, Ornstein–Uhlenbeck (OU) processes, Lévy jump processes, and branching processes—capture complementary aspects of these dynamics but have largely been developed as separate methodological frameworks. We present the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck–Lévy–Branching (OULB) framework, a unified probabilistic model for multiscale biological evolution that integrates continuous dynamics, discontinuous jumps, branch-associated regime dynamics, therapy-dependent attractor shifts, and observation models within a common latent-state representation. Brownian motion provides an unconstrained diffusion baseline, while classical OU, treatment-shifted OU, OU–Lévy, and OU–Branching models arise as nested or constrained formulations within the broader framework. Using a comprehensive simulation platform, we demonstrate generally reliable recovery of continuous stochastic parameters, condition-dependent recovery of jump events and branch-associated regime structure, and improved parameter estimation under sparse, noisy, and irregularly sampled observations. Independent predictive model comparison further delineates the conditions under which candidate dynamical mechanisms can be distinguished and shows reduced discrimination with sparse sampling, increased measurement noise, temporal confounding, and model misspecification. We further introduce an empirical calibration strategy that derives simulation settings from longitudinal cancer evolution data, enabling biologically grounded methodological evaluation. A modular computational workflow integrates simulation, Bayesian inference, calibration, visualization, and uncertainty quantification. The OULB framework establishes a unified mathematical and computational foundation for interpretable, extensible, and reproducible probabilistic modeling across longitudinal, spatial, and multimodal biological systems.

papers.title: Weak-strong uniqueness for the coupled Maxwell and inertial Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equations
papers.abstract: The coupled Maxwell and inertial Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equations are considered with initial data and inhomogeneity supported in a bounded domain. In the interior domain, the time-dependent inertial Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation is coupled with Maxwell interior equations and Maxwell boundary integral equations. We prove that if a strong solution of the coupled system exists for some time interval, it must coincide with every weak solution on that interval. In contrast to earlier results, the present analysis incorporates inertial effects and the coupling with the space-dependent form of Maxwell boundary integral equations. Moreover, our proof accounts for all physically relevant lower-order terms appearing in the inertial Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation, including an applied field, uniaxial anisotropy, a stray field, and the Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interaction. We present an illustrative physics-informed neural network experiment whose training histories and computed field distributions complement the uniqueness result.

papers.title: Slack-based stochastic Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: This article introduces a Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework that leverages a pair of complementary slack variables to quantify constraint violation and robustness, enabling linear probabilistic constraint enforcement. Central to this approach is the definition of an interpretable slack ratio that serves as a monotonic proxy for the violation probability under a mild stochastic-ordering assumption that admits decision-dependent dispersion of the constraint margin, beyond additive-disturbance settings. For location–scale distributions (e.g., Gaussian, Uniform, Laplace), this ratio is invariant to the disturbance mean and variance for a fixed violation probability. We exploit this property to pre-compute low-complexity safety margins that guarantee constraint satisfaction with high confidence at the first prediction step—and along the whole horizon for disturbance families closed under convolution, e.g., the Gaussian case—eliminating the need for online variance estimation. Simulation results demonstrate the applicability of the proposed method in practical problems.

papers.title: Physiological digital twins require cross-system observation contracts
papers.abstract: Whole-body models explain how organ systems can be represented and coupled. A model that is updated repeatedly from patient measurements must also specify when those measurements support a particular conclusion. This Hypothesis and Theory article proposes an Observation Contract Framework: a declared set of evidence requirements for each output, checked whenever that output is requested. Each system uses 10 fields covering target states, direct measurements, proxies, unmeasured states, events, reference measurements, timing, quality failures, prohibited conclusions and measurement readiness. The framework returns permit, degrade or block for each output. Five testable hypotheses address unsupported conclusions, timing errors, missing reference measurements, cross-system dependencies and the distinction between signal reconstruction and state validation. The framework is specified for eight peripheral systems, with central nervous system dependencies explicitly left unobserved. A mathematical oxygen-delivery example explains how system requirements are combined. A small retrospective replay of public critical-care records then illustrates the same rules: a record-based oxygen-delivery proxy can be restricted or withheld as haemoglobin measurements become outdated, while a validated physiological oxygen-delivery claim remains blocked. This replay is an application example, not a clinical validation or a comparative test of the hypotheses. Existing sensors support many bounded measurements, but do not continuously identify regional perfusion, venous capacitance, ventilation–perfusion mismatch, endocrine pulsatility, tissue immune activity or in vivo coagulation potential. The framework complements context-of-use definition, observability and identifiability analysis, model interoperability, verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification. Its purpose is to state what evidence is needed for a conclusion and what must be withheld when that evidence is insufficient.

papers.title: Peer Instruction in Hybrid Computing Courses: The Relationships Between Student Modality, Discussion, and Learning
papers.abstract: Background: Peer instruction is an active learning pedagogy that emphasizes collaboration and learning from one’s peers. Prior research in computing education has shown that using peer instruction can improve students’ learning, reduce dropout and failure rates, and result in larger increases in students’ self-efficacy relative to standard lecture-based instruction. However, it has not investigated the use of peer instruction in hybrid courses, which have become increasingly popular in higher education due to their flexibility and ability to manage increases in enrollment. Objectives: We evaluated the effectiveness of peer instruction at facilitating students’ learning of computing concepts in in-person and online modalities of a hybrid course. Additionally, we examined how students’ discussions between rounds of peer instruction relate to their learning of computing concepts and whether these relationships vary when courses follow different attendance policies. Context and Methods: We analyzed students’ normalized learning gains from peer instruction in two offerings of a hybrid undergraduate data science course where students could choose to attend class meetings in person or synchronously online. In the first (open-policy) offering, students could self-select their modality for each class meeting and alternate modalities at will. In the second (closed-policy) offering, students needed to obtain instructor permission each time they wanted to attend class online, which drastically reduced the proportion of students who did so. Findings: Students who attended class online in the open-policy offering experienced smaller normalized learning gains than students who attended class in person in either offering. Additionally, in the open-policy offering, students who discussed the peer instruction questions in person experienced higher normalized learning gains than students who engaged in discussion online. Lastly, students who engaged in in-person discussion in the open-policy offering experienced higher normalized learning gains than students who did so in the closed-policy offering. Implications: Our results suggest that peer instruction may be more effective in person as opposed to online, particularly if there are differences in discussion environments across modalities. Additionally, they provide insight into how students’ discussion behaviors are related to their modalities. We encourage other instructors to take them into consideration when designing and implementing peer instruction in a hybrid computing course.

papers.title: Fault Diagnosis of Reciprocating Compressor Crosshead Nut Loosening Using Swin Transformer-Based Ordered Transfer Learning
papers.abstract: The connecting nut between the piston rod and the crosshead is a key fastener of reciprocating compressors, and its loosening may lead to unplanned shutdowns and even safety accidents. Fault severities are commonly divided into normal, slight, moderate and severe states, but accurate data-driven diagnosis under variable working conditions remains difficult because labeled experimental fault data are scarce and the fault features of different severities are separated in scale. This paper proposes the Swin Transformer Deep Ordered Transfer Network with Multi-Scale Feature Fusion, CORAL Alignment and Ordinal Regression (Swin-MCO). The source domain is a rigid-flexible coupled multibody simulation validated against bench measurements, and the target domain is a test-bench dataset covering 25 speed and pressure conditions, of which only 20% are labeled for training. The model extracts hierarchical features from 224 × 224 angular-domain texture images, aligns second-order statistics across domains and encodes the physical fault progression in the classifier. The diagnosis accuracies reach 95.80%, 95.57% and 96.72% on the three unseen test sets, and misclassifications are confined to adjacent severity levels. The results indicate that the proposed model provides an effective solution for cross-domain diagnosis of connecting nut loosening. Future work will focus on industrial deployment, lightweight edge implementation and uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: Mapping Middens: Multimodal Imagery Illuminates Rhino Space Use in Savanna Landscapes
papers.abstract: Ecosystem engineering by many animal species creates distinct features across landscapes that shape biodiversity and ecosystem structure and serve as key signatures of animal space use. Remote sensing has been used to map the spatial distributions of such features across landscapes, enhancing our ability to characterize the biotic factors that create resource heterogeneity. However, some animal‐engineered features are challenging to reliably detect even with high‐resolution remotely sensed imagery, limiting our understanding of how ecosystem engineering shapes ecological processes and animal spatial behavior. In African savannas, communal dung middens created by rhinos are central to olfactory communication and nutrient redistribution, but their spatial distribution and the environmental factors shaping midden placement have not been quantified. We used coincident high‐resolution thermal, RGB, and LiDAR data to detect and map rhino middens in Kruger National Park, South Africa, and demonstrate that active learning using multimodal imagery can efficiently detect middens across large areas. We then analyzed midden spatial patterning and used remotely sensed habitat metrics to quantify drivers of midden placement across spatial scales. Although we found weak and inconsistent deviations from complete spatial randomness in midden spatial patterning, midden placement was not random but strongly associated with proximity to or density of animal paths, proximity to water, and low levels of vegetation cover. These midden sites likely offer ease of access in areas of high rhino traffic that further facilitates the broadcasting of social cues. We found no relationship between midden placement and terrain attributes, suggesting that middens are placed throughout the topographic landscape, providing new insights into rhino space use. We demonstrate how using multimodal remote sensing data can facilitate a scalable approach to detecting cryptic animal‐made features in heterogeneous landscapes, providing a foundation for studying broad‐scale impacts of overlooked ecosystem engineering features that can be used to inform conservation strategy.

papers.title: Motion planning and control integrated with LLM for unstructured terrain with slope restrictions
papers.abstract: To address the core challenges of autonomous driving motion planning in complex unstructured environments, this paper proposes an integrated solution that combines slope constraints, large language model parameter optimization, and large language model obstacle avoidance decision-making. First, a slope-aware 3D Hybrid A* path planning algorithm with a multi-objective cost function and an optimized heuristic function is proposed. Secondly, an adaptive parameter optimization framework integrating Hybrid A* with Large Language Model (LLM) is developed, dynamically adjusting key parameters through a closed-loop mechanism. Finally, an LLM-assisted model predictive control (MPC) scheme for trajectory tracking and obstacle avoidance is developed, which achieves a balanced trade-off between tracking accuracy and collision safety. The proposed obstacle avoidance method is compared with alternative approaches.

papers.title: PHYSICS-INFORMED NEURAL NETWORK-BASED SENSORLESS SPEED ESTIMATION OF BRUSHLESS DIRECT CURRENT MOTOR DRIVE
papers.abstract: Brushless direct current (BLDC) motors are employed for electric vehicles (EVs), medical equipment, and military robots because of their fast dynamic speed response and wide range of speed regulation characteristics. However, conventional methods are not suitable for dynamic speed-varying conditions, which leads to parameter variation issues and longer computational time. Therefore, in this article, a novel Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) for sensorless speed detection of a BLDC motor is implemented using a machine learning-based physics-informed neural network (PINN) algorithm. Variables obtained from the PINN training are incorporated into the novel EKF; then, with the implemented model, the BLDC motor speed tracks the reference speed in dynamic, speed-varying conditions, thereby eliminating parameter variation issues and achieving shorter computational time as well. The implemented sensorless speed estimation scheme is compared with the conventional algorithms, and the results are presented using LAUNCHXL-F28379D. Also, compared with other conventional sensorless speed estimation techniques, the implemented method achieved reduced speed errors of 0.003% and 0.03% at 1500 rpm and 2000 rpm, respectively.

papers.title: Medial Malleolar Cortical Thickening with Non metallic implants for Prophylactic fixation in Total Ankle Arthroplasty.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Metal and non-metal fixation has long been utilized in orthopedic procedures but carries drawbacks including migration, breakage, osteolysis, imaging interference, and potential need for removal. Although absorbable hardware has historically shown mixed results, advancements in bio-integrative technology promise non-metal alternatives that reduce stress shielding and support healing. Periprosthetic fracturing in the setting of total ankle arthroplasty (TAA) is an area of high concern which can lead to severe clinical ramifications. PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to assess changes in medial malleolar thickness in TAA specifically comparing use of integrative technology to a control. STUDY DESIGN/METHODS: The authors reviewed a single surgeon operative database of patients who underwent primary total ankle replacement (TAR) between December 2018 and February 2024 with a minimum of 1 year follow up. Ninety-one subjects that underwent TAA were included in this study. RESULTS: We found a statistically significant increase in cortical thickness post-operatively in the group who had prophylactic fixation of the medial malleolus with the bio-integrative implant compared to preoperative cortical thickness, with an average increase of 0.63 cm (p-value < 0.0001). However, this finding did not demonstrate an association with the incidence of medial malleolar stress fractures. CONCLUSION: Although biointegrative prophylactic fixation was associated with increased medial malleolar cortical thickness following TAA, the clinical significance of this finding remains uncertain. Further studies are warranted to determine whether biointegrative fixation provides meaningful protection against medial malleolar stress fractures. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 3, retrospective cohort study.

papers.title: Transcriptomic Characterization of Early Osseointegration: An Exploratory In Vivo RNA-Seq Study.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: This exploratory in vivo RNA-seq study investigated early molecular responses at the bone-implant interface of commercially available titanium (Ti) dental implants using a rabbit tibia model at 10 days post-implantation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Three screw-shaped (4.0 mm × 8.0 mm) implant types were prepared: (1) turned Ti, (2) SLA-modified Ti, and (3) turned copper (Cu). Four sites-including a drilled Sham control-were placed in the tibiae of four New Zealand white rabbits. Surface roughness parameters and chemical composition were evaluated (n = 3). Histomorphometric analysis was performed to assess bone-to-implant contact (BIC) and bone area (BA). Peri-implant tissue was harvested for RNA extraction and sequenced using the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform. Transcriptome-wide differential gene expression analysis was performed, followed by gene ontology (GO) enrichment analysis. Multiple-testing correction was performed using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) method. RESULTS: Both Ti groups yielded significantly higher BIC and BA than Cu (P < .001). Transcriptome-wide analysis identified 28 differentially expressed genes (FDR-adjusted P < .05, log₂(fold change) > 1 or < -1), which clustered into three functional categories: pro-inflammatory mediators, immunoregulatory/innate defense responses, and mitochondrial/stress-related pathways. SLA Ti showed a transcriptional pattern suggestive of coordinated immune-related signaling (increased expression of TNF, IL 1α, Gal-3, ORM1, and S100A6), whereas turned Cu exhibited upregulation of mitochondrial and oxidative stress-related genes alongside reduced antioxidant and innate defense markers. Notably, no genes met the differential expression criteria in the SLA Ti versus turned Ti comparison. CONCLUSIONS: This exploratory RNA-seq study identified distinct transcriptional profiles during early peri-implant healing. The findings provide preliminary insight into molecular events occurring at the bone-implant interface and may serve as a foundation for future studies investigating the biology of osseointegration.

papers.title: Seventeen-Year Follow-up of Migrated Dental Implants with a Prosthesis: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Long-term migration of osseointegrated dental implants is a rare clinical phenomenon. This case report describes a 17-year follow-up of a patient who experienced implant migration more than a decade after functional loading. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A 58-year-old female patient with advanced periodontal disease underwent comprehensive implant therapy. Following full-mouth extractions except for teeth 34 and 43, six implants were placed in the maxilla and six in the mandible. A maxillary cross-arch implant-supported fixed partial denture (IS-FPD) and three mandibular IS-FPDs (at sites 36-35, 33-42, and 44-46) were delivered. After 12 years of stable function, migration of implants at sites 33 and 42, along with adjacent teeth 34 and 43 and their prosthesis, was identified. Following the extraction of the adjacent natural teeth, a new mandibular cross-arch prosthesis was fabricated over the existing, stable implants. RESULTS: Despite the multi-directional migration, the migrated implants maintained the stability without any mechanical or structural failure. The patient was monitored for an additional 5 years (17 years of total follow-up), during which the implants remained stable in their new clinical positions without further complications. CONCLUSIONS: Re-prosthetic intervention can achieve long-term functional stability for migrated dental implants. Non-surgical prosthetic approach implies an optional treatment strategy for managing long-term implant migration while preserving the function under the clinical and radiographic stability compatible with osseointegration.

papers.title: Effects of Cover Screw and Healing Abutment on Early Implant Stability: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: This randomized split-mouth controlled clinical trial compared the effects of a cover screw and a healing abutment on implant stability during early osseointegration. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Systemically healthy individuals requiring at least two dental implants were included in this split-mouth study; one implant received a healing abutment (one-stage protocol) and the contralateral implant a cover screw (two-stage protocol). Treatment allocation was randomized using sealed opaque envelopes. Primary implant stability was assessed by insertion torque and resonance frequency analysis. Implant Stability Quotient (ISQ) values were recorded at baseline and at 3-month follow-up, and changes in implant stability (ΔISQ) were analysed. The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07687615). RESULTS: The study included 46 systemically healthy individuals. No significant differences were observed between the groups with respect to baseline ISQ values or insertion torque (p>0.05). However, both the 3-month ISQ values and ΔISQ were significantly greater in the cover screw group than in the healing abutment group (p<0.05). The mean 3-month ISQ value was 77.77±3.14 in the cover screw group and 75.63±5.03 in the healing abutment group (p=0.001). Baseline insertion torque was positively correlated with the 3-month ISQ values in both protocols (p<0.001). CONCLUSION: Submerged healing with a cover screw resulted in a modest but statistically significant increase in the secondary implant stability. However, because the absolute inter-group difference was small and both groups achieved mean ISQ values above 70, no clinically significant advantage of either protocol was detected during the 3-month follow-up period.
